purpose: Harden the existing Workday specification coverage by binding one customer-configured worker export and one effective-dated read-only worker snapshot to the same tenant, connection, regional host, schema, source window, record count and integration event before admitting reconciliation evidence.

overrides.reason: Workday documents a current versioned SOAP directory, REST services, OAuth security, Core Connector: Worker, connector change detection, customer-configured integration systems and unique integration event IDs; VECTOR now composes those boundaries into count-only worker reconciliation evidence without gaining worker or payroll mutation authority.

connectionRoutes: customer-configured Core Connector: Worker with a dedicated integration system and approved delivery endpoint
tenant-specific HTTPS Workday Web Services Human Resources Get_Workers read surface where separately entitled
tenant-specific Workday REST API with OAuth 2.0 and the Workday configurable security model where the required worker resource is available
RaaS or SFTP worker export only when its exact report, fields, parameters, encryption and delivery route are customer approved
readRoutes: Core Connector: Worker full or change-detection output with exact integration system identity
Workday Web Services Human Resources Get_Workers on a pinned supported production WWS version
approved Workday REST Person, Staffing, Absence, Time Tracking or Payroll resources as separate least-privilege datasets
approved RaaS custom report with immutable report identity, schema and parameters
integration event and Process Monitor evidence for exact launch-to-completion tracking
deniedMutationRoutes: Put_Worker and all worker create, update, terminate, rescind, transfer or staffing business-process actions
payroll calculation, result, payment, tax, time, absence, schedule, benefit or compensation mutation
integration system, security group, domain permission, API client, report, delivery or endpoint reconfiguration
inbound EIB, connector, SOAP, REST, Studio or Orchestrate writes
checkpoint, deletion, attendance, payroll, operational or causal authority
dataObjects: employment, position, job, company, supervisory organisation, location and cost-centre assignments
effective dates, source versions and customer-selected worker fields
integration systems, integration event IDs, run status, record counts, page or file manifests and delivery outcomes
schema, mapping, credential, freshness, completeness and reconciliation diagnostics
stableIdentifiers: Workday tenant name scopes every tenant-specific endpoint and export
Workday ID (WID) and approved reference IDs remain opaque source identifiers
worker, employment and position identifiers remain separate so concurrent jobs are not collapsed
integration system ID identifies the configured connector
integration event ID is unique per invocation and is hashed before VECTOR evidence leaves the connector boundary
freshnessLatency: integration systems can be launched manually, on a schedule, by API, subscription or business process
Core Connector change detection is distinct from date-range filtering and depends on connector-specific transaction-log and effective-date rules
full snapshots remain the safe bootstrap and periodic reconciliation route
freshness is measured from the exact source window, integration event completion and VECTOR observation time
permissions: integration systems define launch security and execution rights
Workday configurable security governs REST resources and tenant data
SOAP and connector access is restricted to the exact required Get/read domains and approved fields
customer-owned integration configuration remains separate from VECTOR runtime authority
the normal VECTOR connector cannot configure reports, integrations, endpoints, security groups or worker records
paginationDeltaWebhooks: Core Connector output is reconciled using a completed integration event plus a gapless file/page manifest
direct SOAP or REST paging is enabled only after the tenant proves the exact page/result contract for the pinned resource and version
connector change detection is not inferred from start/end-date filters
full worker snapshots and change-detection outputs use separate checkpoint namespaces and are never silently interchanged
no notification or event signal is accepted as complete worker state without an authenticated read or completed export
regionalApiVersions: tenant-specific Workday HTTPS host is discovered from authorised customer configuration and bound exactly
WWS v47.0 is documented for Workday 2026R2 and earlier supported production versions remain separately listed
REST service versions are resource-specific and cannot be represented as one account-wide API version
preview WWS definitions are not production contracts and cannot replace a pinned production version
regional failover never silently changes tenant host, data location or checkpoint namespace
customFields: Core Connector: Worker integration maps, attributes and field overrides are customer configurable
RaaS fields and calculated fields remain bound to an approved report and schema fingerprint
customer-specific IDs and local fields remain source-attributed extensions until explicitly mapped
field addition, removal, type, sensitivity or effective-date semantic changes trigger schema review
rateLimits: public documentation reviewed does not establish one universal worker API limit across SOAP, REST, RaaS and connector exports
tenant-proven limits, timeouts and concurrency are connection policy and evidence bound
throttling or service unavailability uses bounded backoff without widening identity, version, field or date scope
large estates partition safe reads by company or approved organisation only when the source contract preserves complete scope
failureModes: connector reports completed but a delivery step or external endpoint did not receive the file
integration event ID, integration system, tenant host, company, schema or source window does not match the approved connection
Core Connector transaction-log or change-detection configuration is missing or changed
date filtering is incorrectly treated as change detection
partial, gapped, duplicated, reordered or count-inconsistent output manifests
one worker with multiple employment or position assignments is collapsed into one identity
future-dated, corrected or concurrently effective worker slices overwrite one another
WWS or REST version, response groups, RaaS fields, maps or integration attributes drift
OAuth expiry, insufficient domain permissions, tenant-host change, timeout, throttling, regional outage or delivery failure
secret, credential, raw worker ID or executable data enters evidence
reconciliation: bind Workday tenant, VECTOR tenant, connection, company, regional host, export, WWS version, Get_Workers query, schema and source window
require a completed zero-error integration event and gapless export manifest
require a complete effective-dated worker snapshot over the exact same source window
require export and parsed worker record counts to agree
preserve person, employment and assignment identities independently and retain sequence-numbered corrections
hash Workday tenant and integration event identity and return only counts and evidence fingerprints
never infer deletion from this evidence or advance a checkpoint without the durable checkpoint owner
never grant worker, attendance, payroll, write-back, operational or causal authority
schemaDrift: pin WWS or REST resource version, response groups, export revision, approved fields, query, schema, map and scope fingerprints
quarantine preview-to-production changes, removed fields, sensitive-field additions, type changes and report or connector reconfiguration
preserve the original schema and export revision with historical evidence so replay is interpreted against the contract that produced it
retriesReconnect: refresh OAuth only within the approved Workday API client and security domain where REST is used
retry a failed read or export only inside the same tenant, integration, version, field set and source window
use Process Monitor and integration event evidence to distinguish launch, processing and delivery failures
run a complete read-only worker snapshot after a missed, ambiguous or reconfigured change-detection window
require customer-controlled repair when integration configuration, security domains, report definitions or delivery endpoints change
customerValueOpportunities: prevent missing, duplicated or stale worker assignments from driving unsafe schedules, overtime, access or payroll preparation
preserve concurrent jobs and positions so skills, availability, cost centre and site decisions use the correct assignment
distinguish a genuine workforce change from a failed Workday launch, connector configuration or delivery step
reduce implementation effort by reusing Core Connector: Worker, approved RaaS or Get_Workers rather than bespoke point-to-point exports
preserve effective history for planned-versus-realised staffing and outcome analysis without pretending correlation is causation
zeroFrictionConnection: discover tenant host, supported production WWS versions and existing worker integrations from authorised configuration
propose Core Connector: Worker as the default enterprise export and a minimum approved worker field set
pre-fill tenant, integration system, company, export revision, source window, schema and delivery route
test one bounded non-production export without creating or modifying a worker
measure configuration questions, manual field mappings, retries and time-to-first-reconciled worker snapshot removed
patch.productHandoff: Show one assignment-aware workforce source-health card: last reconciled worker snapshot, integration event state, expected versus parsed rows, freshness, affected company/site, multi-job collision count and exact failure layer. Do not show raw WIDs or imply payroll, attendance or worker approval.
patch.autonomyHandoff: Detect tenant-host drift, OAuth or domain-permission failure, integration-event failure, connector configuration drift, missing delivery, count mismatch, multi-job collision and stale snapshots. Auto-recover only by bounded token refresh, exact-window read retry or an already-authorised worker export; otherwise prepare the precise customer-controlled repair.
patch.evidenceNote: Official Workday documentation reviewed 2026-09-28. No Workday tenant, customer Core Connector, OAuth client, ISU, live Get_Workers call, worker export, delivery, reconciliation, denied mutation, hosted VECTOR proof or provider certification is claimed.
patch.nextBuildAction: Use an authorised Workday non-production tenant to prove the exact tenant host and security domains, one Core Connector: Worker or Get_Workers full snapshot, integration event completion, delivery manifest, multi-job/effective-date mapping, count reconciliation, OAuth expiry, permission denial, connector drift, delivery failure, throttling and denied worker/payroll mutations.
